note: Original PersonalityDNA descriptive text. Bands refer to position on the response scale, not comparison with other people. No trait level is better or worse overall; each has typical advantages and trade-offs.

openness.name: Openness
openness.short: Curiosity, imagination and interest in ideas and new experiences.

lower.summary: You describe yourself as preferring the practical, concrete and familiar.
strengths: Valuing what has proven to work
growth: Try one unfamiliar idea or activity each week and note what you learn

middle.summary: You describe a mix of practicality and curiosity, depending on the situation.
growth: Notice which situations draw out your curiosity, and seek more of them where useful

higher.summary: You describe yourself as curious, imaginative and drawn to ideas and new experiences.
growth: Choose which ideas to pursue to completion
Translate abstract ideas into concrete examples for others

lower.summary: You describe yourself as flexible and spontaneous, with less emphasis on order and schedules.
growth: Use one simple tool, such as a short daily list, for the commitments that matter most

middle.summary: You describe a balance between structure and flexibility.
strengths: Organised when it matters, relaxed when it does not
growth: Identify the areas where more structure would help you most

higher.summary: You describe yourself as organised, prepared and attentive to detail.
growth: Allow room for change in plans
Notice when high standards cost more than they return

extraversion.name: Extraversion
extraversion.short: Sociability, assertiveness and energy from social interaction.

lower.summary: You describe yourself as quieter and more reserved, often preferring smaller settings.
growth: Plan how you will share your views in group settings
Protect time to recharge

middle.summary: You describe yourself as comfortable both with people and on your own.
strengths: Adapting to social and solitary settings
growth: Notice which settings energise you and which tire you

higher.summary: You describe yourself as outgoing, talkative and comfortable being noticed.
growth: Leave pauses for others to contribute
Practise reflective listening

agreeableness.name: Agreeableness
agreeableness.short: Warmth, empathy, cooperation and consideration for others.

lower.summary: You describe yourself as more direct and independent-minded, with less focus on others' feelings.
growth: Ask about others' perspectives before giving your view

middle.summary: You describe a balance between consideration for others and standing your ground.
growth: Notice when you tend to accommodate and when you tend to push back

higher.summary: You describe yourself as warm, caring and attentive to other people's feelings.
growth: Practise stating your own needs clearly
Set boundaries when helping others

emotional_stability.name: Emotional Stability
emotional_stability.short: How calm and even-tempered you describe yourself in everyday situations. The reverse direction is called Negative Emotionality (Neuroticism).

lower.summary: You describe yourself as experiencing everyday stress and emotional ups and downs fairly often.
growth: Try a short routine for stressful moments, such as pausing to name what you feel
If stress feels overwhelming, consider speaking with a qualified professional

middle.summary: You describe a typical mix of calm and stress in everyday life.
strengths: Responsive to situations without being overwhelmed by them
growth: Notice which situations tend to unsettle you, and plan for them

higher.summary: You describe yourself as calm and relaxed in most everyday situations.
growth: Check in on how others are feeling, which may differ from your own calm
